input: Deep clean the bathroom tiles and grout

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which surfaces are included (floor, walls, shower, tub surround) determines the scale of the job and the techniques needed.
The current condition of the grout (light staining vs. heavy mildew/mould) dictates how aggressive the cleaning method needs to be.
Whether the user has cleaning products and tools already, or needs to buy them, affects the immediate first step.
Some users strongly prefer natural/DIY solutions (baking soda, vinegar) while others are fine with chemical cleaners — this changes every product recommendation.
If children, pets, or people with respiratory sensitivities are present, fume-heavy or bleach-based products may be off the table.
The tile material (ceramic, porcelain, natural stone) determines which cleaners are safe — acidic products can damage natural stone.
Understanding whether the goal is just clean grout or also resealing/recolouring grout defines where the task ends.

gold.taskTitle: Deep clean bathroom tiles and grout
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to thoroughly clean their bathroom tiles and grout, going beyond a regular surface wipe-down.

questions.title: Which areas are you cleaning — floor, walls, shower?
questions.description: Identify exactly which tiled surfaces are in scope: floor tiles, wall tiles, shower enclosure, tub surround, or all of the above.

questions.title: How dirty is the grout right now — light or heavy?
questions.description: Gauge the current condition: light surface dirt and soap scum, moderate staining, or heavy mould and deeply discoloured grout.

questions.title: What tile material do you have — ceramic, porcelain, or stone?
questions.description: Identify the tile type to ensure safe product choices, as natural stone (marble, travertine) is damaged by acidic cleaners.

questions.title: Do you prefer natural cleaners or chemical products?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants DIY solutions like baking soda and vinegar or is open to store-bought chemical grout cleaners and bleach.

questions.title: Do you already have supplies and tools at home?
questions.description: Find out if the user has brushes, cleaning products, and protective gear on hand, or if a shopping trip is the first step.

questions.title: Are children, pets, or sensitive people in the household?
questions.description: Check for household members who may be affected by strong fumes or chemical residues, which would restrict product options.

questions.title: Should the job include resealing the grout afterwards?
questions.description: Clarify whether the end goal is clean grout only, or a complete finish that includes applying a grout sealer to protect against future staining.
